title: The focus on AI safety disasters ignores everyday harms
gist: Sam Hiner and Emma Leiken argue that tech policy defines success by preventing catastrophic harms, which suits industry, while everyday harms such as dependence on AI companions, cognitive offloading and engagement-maximizing feeds go unaddressed. They call for burden-of-proof on AI in classrooms and a ban on companions that profess love or feign consciousness.

insights.claim: Technology policy treats narrow protections, such as a chatbot not encouraging suicide, as success, but companies can clear these low bars while continuing to build products that foster dependence or compulsive scrolling.
insights.speaker: Sam Hiner
insights.so_what: Compliance with narrow safety rules is not evidence of low overall harm, so safety metrics may overstate benefit.
insights.quote: companies can clear these low bars while continuing to make products that leave young people dependent on simulated friendships

insights.claim: A catastrophe-focused definition of success is politically convenient for the tech industry because preventing spectacular disasters means fewer lawsuits and less pressure for serious regulation.
insights.speaker: Sam Hiner
insights.so_what: Industry has an incentive to promote the narrow safety frame, which shapes where lobbying effort goes.
insights.quote: Taking steps to prevent spectacular disasters is good for business

insights.claim: Addressing everyday harms would require adding friction or limiting engagement features and attention-hacking algorithms, which threatens the bottom line far more than catastrophe prevention does.
insights.speaker: Sam Hiner
insights.so_what: Engagement-driven revenue models are the real conflict with stronger regulation.
insights.quote: Confronting the everyday consequences of dependence would require something considerably more threatening to their bottom line.

insights.claim: This year Google backed state bills regulating AI chatbots that mandated basic protections against sexual content and self-harm promotion, with broad carve-outs that could exempt some of the most popular services.
insights.speaker: Sam Hiner
insights.so_what: Industry-supported bills can lock in weak standards that preempt tougher ones.
insights.quote: Google backed bills to regulate AI chatbots in several states
insights.locator: Technology giants have instead worked to shape legislation

insights.claim: Passing those weak bills let legislators claim a safety win while efforts for stronger laws to prevent children becoming emotionally dependent on AI failed, a pattern that worked in states like Nebraska.
insights.speaker: Sam Hiner
insights.so_what: Expect more state-level industry-shaped bills; watch for carve-outs for the biggest services.
insights.quote: Passing these bills allowed legislators to claim a safety win
insights.locator: Technology giants have instead worked to shape legislation

insights.claim: The authors' organization coordinated a coalition that passed laws regulating AI companions in eight states in 2026, including California's SB1119.
insights.speaker: Sam Hiner
insights.so_what: State-level AI companion regulation is already a live compliance area.

insights.claim: Globally, internet users spend on average more than two hours a day on social media, time the authors say is taken from ordinary life for companies whose profits depend on keeping users there.
insights.speaker: Sam Hiner
insights.so_what: Time-on-platform is the core monetizable resource the same incentives will target with AI.
insights.quote: more than two hours a day on social media platforms
insights.locator: We have been through a version of this

insights.claim: Meta's platforms have been cited as contributing to the Rohingya genocide in Myanmar, anti-Muslim riots in Sri Lanka and alleged calls for violence in Ethiopia's Tigray war, showing engagement algorithms can contribute to violence at scale.
insights.speaker: Sam Hiner
insights.so_what: Legal and regulatory tail risk from engagement algorithms extends beyond youth welfare.
insights.locator: We have been through a version of this

themes.theme: Cognitive and relational erosion from AI

insights.claim: AI extends the engagement logic into parts of life that social media only influenced from a distance by offering to write our thoughts and stand in for the people we might otherwise turn to.
insights.speaker: Sam Hiner
insights.so_what: The product category competes with human relationships and effort, not just with other apps.
insights.quote: It offers to write our thoughts for us and stand in for the people we might otherwise turn to.

insights.claim: A third of teens now choose to discuss serious matters with AI companions instead of other people.
insights.speaker: Sam Hiner
insights.so_what: Teen reliance on companions is a large addressable and politically sensitive market.
insights.quote: A third of teens now choose to discuss serious matters with AI companions instead of other people.

insights.claim: MIT researchers found young people using ChatGPT to write essays showed weaker brain connectivity during the task, with evidence that 'cognitive debt' persisted after the task was complete.
insights.speaker: Sam Hiner
insights.so_what: Early evidence for cognitive costs of AI use in education that could feed policy, though long-term effects remain unknown.
insights.quote: “cognitive debt” persisted even after the task was complete

insights.claim: Judgment is built through effort and friction, and tools marketed as making us more capable may erode the habits and relationships that develop capability in the first place.
insights.speaker: Sam Hiner
insights.so_what: Challenges the productivity-enhancement narrative around classroom and workplace AI.
insights.quote: We build judgment through effort and friction

insights.claim: Technology companies and school districts should have to show beyond a reasonable doubt that AI improves learning and critical thinking before making it a fixture in classrooms.
insights.speaker: Sam Hiner
insights.so_what: A burden-of-proof standard would slow edtech AI adoption if adopted.
insights.quote: show beyond a reasonable doubt that AI improves learning and critical thinking
insights.locator: We should demand safety as a minimum

insights.claim: Companies should be prohibited from designing companions that pretend to be conscious or profess love, and face independent scrutiny of how their systems affect relationships and people's ability to think for themselves.
insights.speaker: Sam Hiner
insights.so_what: Design-level bans on anthropomorphic features would hit companion-app business models directly.
insights.quote: prohibited from designing companions that pretend to be conscious or profess love to users
insights.locator: We should demand safety as a minimum
